01 / UI Improvements

A wider battlefield,
with key information close at hand.

Combat has moved from an opponent's portrait and text to a screen where you choose your actions while viewing their full-body artwork and the battlefield.

2.4.1

A redesigned combat screen

Full-body artwork and the background fill the center, with combatant status, actions, and weapon techniques arranged on either side. The combat log below spans the central panel, giving you more room to read.

  • Choose separately between attacking, defending, using potions, switching weapons, and each weapon's techniques.
  • Scroll through longer combat logs, with attack highlighting and left-aligned text preserved.
  • Distinct hit effects identify piercing, slashing, blunt, and mental attacks.
  • Victory and defeat indicators and the continue button sit outside the message, making results easier to read.
2.4.0 → 2.4.1

Traits in one place, with clearer descriptions

The full trait overview lets you browse discovered dispositions and titles and read their descriptions. Distinct grade colors, title colors, and description formatting help you make training decisions.

Since 2.4.0

Find stored characters by face

Cryo cells display each character's face and name. Browse through pages to find someone in storage, with less need to search a list from memory alone.

2.4.0 → 2.4.1

Updated tutorials and introductions

The tutorial now uses the latest shared layout. Expanded descriptions of places and people help you understand where you are and whom you've met.

02 / Artwork Remaster

From the city streets
to a duel's final moments.

Expanded regional and facility backgrounds, major character art and portraits, full-body combat art, and defeat scenes. This complete edition brings together base-game, Indie Patch, personal, and additional artwork.

Previous asset
Replacement asset

A comparison of the previous and replacement backgrounds for the same location. The image on the left is the previous asset, not a screenshot of version 2.3.

2.4.1

A battlefield for each setting

Each setting has its own atmosphere: a misty forest at the Fog Border, a spectator-lined arena, and a torchlit underground fighting pit at the Catfight Club.

2.4.1

Monsters in scale, characters in arms

Composition and backgrounds convey the size of giant enemies, while smaller foes are scaled to the surrounding terrain. Major characters' weapons and combat appearances have been brought in line with their established roles.

2.4.1

Combat and defeat as a set

Full-body combat art is paired with defeat scenes, and group opponents have scenes showing their defeat together. Some monsters also have distinct appearances at different growth stages.

There are new ways to enjoy the artwork, too.

Switch between registered original and alternate images and keep your selection. You can also hide the UI to view cutscenes on their own. This edition brings together the selected assets; it does not replace every image with new artwork.

03 / Game System Changes and Additions

Whom will you train,
and whom will you send into battle?

The changes in 2.4 go beyond the screen. Companion combat, individual growth and dialogue, and the choices involved in managing several characters build on the existing flow of training, deliveries, and battles.

Since 2.4.0

Send a slave or assistant into Fog Border combat first

On ordinary Fog Border patrols, you can send one companion into battle first. If they lose, the player character takes over. Damage already dealt, defeated enemies, and resources the enemies have spent are preserved. Each combatant chooses equipment when their turn begins.

Choose a combatantAlone / Slave / Assistant
→
Your companion fights firstUsing their trained abilities and equipment
→
If they lose, the player character takes overDamage dealt to enemies is preserved

This does not send the slave, assistant, and player character into battle in a three-person sequence. Check your companion's condition and action points, and remember that defeat has consequences.

Since 2.4.0 · Further refinements

The same lessons and routines
affect everyone differently.

Personality shapes learning speed, repeated activities, reactions to achievement, and even how unpleasant experiences are remembered. Not every disposition is visible from the start; some traits are discovered through activities.

Genius · SimpletonDifferences in learning speed and growth
Persistent · DistractibleDifferent results from repeated activities
Petty · GenerousDifferent ways of remembering unpleasant experiences
Healthy Constitution · FrailDifferences in fitness and physical training
Berserker · PaladinOffensive and defensive tendencies in battle
Seasoned WarriorA distinct kind of staying power in battle

Track changes through the full trait overview and discovery notices, and manage characters with Constitution Improvement, Chaotic Essence, and more. Special qualities such as Versatile, Peerless Beauty, and Meiki also add value to training and trading.

Since 2.4.0

Beyond first impressions,
conversations about relationships and experience.

Conversation topics now cover the past, impressions, requests, desired activities, dislikes, current mood, and opinions of other characters. Replies vary with personality, speech style, relationships, emotions, and recent experiences.

Recently used wording repeats less often, and longer replies are grouped so that sentences are not cut in the middle. Unique characters' stories and manually written backgrounds are preserved.

Dialogue combines predefined passages to fit the situation. It does not mean thousands of standalone events or unlimited conversation.

Since 2.4.0

Battle experience and personal reputation

Battle experience earned by the characters who actually fight, witness accounts from the Fog Border, and Rally and Catfight Club results now contribute to personal reputation. The results of training show beyond the lesson menus.

Since 2.4.0

Manage several characters across rooms and tasks

Choose a diet for each private room and distinguish shared chores from a private-room maid's duties. Navigation between rooms and storage has also been refined to make characters easier to find.

04 / Balance and Management

Rebalancing the value of training
and the choices you make each day.

How you train a character, where you trade, and how you spend your action points now connect more clearly.

Key adjustments you'll notice in play
AreaWhat changedWhat it means in play
Action points and overworkBase action points adjusted for physical fitness; reduced overwork strain for muscular charactersConsider physical training alongside the way you divide up the day's tasks.
Constitution and growthConstitution traits now affect combat resources and physical training, with improved growth effectsThe same schedule can lead to different training choices depending on a character's constitution.
Character appraisalTrade value reflects current attributes, skills, obedience, overall grade, and special traitsTraining results and individual strengths matter when deciding to sell.
Colosseum rewardsExisting prize tiers increased by the same proportion; results and prize announcements combinedReview the match result and prize money together.
Public auctionsPayment caps removed on Easy and Normal; Hardcore retains caps and explains deductionsAuction payment rules depend on your chosen difficulty.
Since 2.4.0 · Further refinements

Buyer rumors suited to your characters

Local contacts can share buyer rumors suited to the characters you own. When there is no suitable special recommendation, they point you toward a Guild buyback.

Since 2.4.0

Trades that recognize a character's value

Improved the value of Meiki, Peerless Beauty, and Versatile, along with some special trading benefits. NPCs do not all use the same price multiplier; a customer's requirements and available funds still matter.

Since 2.4.0

Ways to respond to a financial crisis

A new sequence lets you respond to a shortage of funds by selling assets or raising money yourself. Housing, decorations, facilities, and owned characters have separate disposal and settlement processes.

You'll need to decide what to keep and what to sell. Actually disposing of a character also has consequences for ongoing quests tied to them.

05 / Cutscenes & Events

The story continues
after victory or defeat.

New artwork is accompanied by connections between match choices, results, and follow-up scenes. Existing major events also have updated presentation to match current appearances and locations.

2.4.1

After victory, decide your opponent's fate

Regular Colosseum matches and ordinary Catfight Club matches lead to a choice to execute or spare your opponent. Artwork and dialogue reflect your decision, while practice matches end as sparring sessions, separate from fights over life and death.

2.4.1

Your conduct can come back to you

Acts of cruelty and mercy build a history. This also affects how opponents treat your characters when they lose in the Colosseum or Catfight Club. The risk of injury in combat still remains.

Distinct scenes for victory, defeat, and what follows

Separate outcomes cover sparring by the player character, slave, or assistant; death, execution, and the evacuation of survivors in regular matches; the defeated opponent's fate; and scenes after becoming champion. Result dialogue has also been refined to connect the finished battle naturally with the next scene.

Isabella's tavern and recruitment scenes now match her current appearance, and combat artwork for Egeya and other major event opponents has been improved. Sequential scenes in the red-light district and salon, plus role outfits for some unique characters, have also been refined.

The Portal Guardian and Vatican Paladin show how introductions and combat presentation have been updated for existing events. They do not indicate newly unlocked regions or separate quests.

06 / Other Changes

Smaller improvements and fixes.

This section collects the smaller adjustments, bug fixes, and features still being expanded, separately from the main content above.

Training, production, and information displays
  • Merged overlapping work, rest, and attention-related dispositions and standardized their current names. Also resolved some cases of incompatible traits appearing together.
  • Improved Meiki discovery history and first-discovery notices, along with certain rare traits' training, production, and cosmetic-surgery benefits.
  • Chaotic Essence now removes eligible negative traits first, followed by ambiguous dispositions. Clearly positive traits and protected entries are retained.
  • Aligned yields, reports, and manual/automatic accounting for certain specialist lessons and production activities, including milk production.
  • Separated the monster's craving/satisfaction indicator from the assistant's personal condition, with growth stages explained separately.
  • Revised attribute, skill, and overall-grade displays, pregnancy-stage and status icons, equipment descriptions, tooltips, and emoji.
  • Ordinary moves preserve private rooms and their occupants. Private-room expansion limits now distinguish between residences.
  • Grouped defeat scenes for group battles and standardized MOB portrait frames, background colors, face placement, and image dimensions.
  • Detailed descriptions now offer contextual hints rather than spelling out exact probabilities, formulas, and reward conditions.
Combat Display, Weapons, and Group Scenes · Fixes
  • Fixed paths that omitted an opponent's full-body image or linked the wrong image in some event battles.
  • Corrected mismatches between enemy weapons, attack messages, and damage types, and restored missing weapon icons in the special skill menu.
  • Fixed individual defeat images overlapping the group victory scene, and corrected image references that gave different monster growth stages the same appearance.
  • Adjusted paths where frames shifted during combat effects, along with the alignment, colors, and line spacing of combat messages.
Catfight Club and Match Results · Fixes
  • Fixed introductions that used a previous character's name instead of the current participant's name.
  • Refined the images and dialogue after execution or mercy choices, and the flow into sparring results for the player character, slave, and assistant.
  • Addressed mismatches between prize messages and actual payments, consolidated the separate prize-only page, and improved the return paths after results.
  • Fixed Catfight Club result images remaining over subsequent activity screens, including bathing, cooking, and cleaning.
Character Information, Private Rooms, and Daily Processing · Fixes
  • Fixed some new traits remaining hidden when using trait-revealing magic or equipment.
  • Fixed ego growth from private room 2 being applied to a character in another room.
  • Improved Egeya's default image selection, full-body image paths for some unique characters, and character image links in Julia-related scenes.
  • Fixed guild-related daily notices appearing blank or extending outside the text panel.
Consignment, Inventory, and Accounting · Fixes
  • Fixed failed returns caused by confusing an auction consignment character with another temporary candidate, along with some duplicate settlements.
  • Fixed some meat production quantities being omitted from the production summary in the accounts.
  • Improved Agrabah shop menus so unavailable products remain visible, making it easier to check why they cannot be purchased.
  • Tidied unnecessary headings and first-line spacing in character and location information panels, along with gold, special inventory, and some menu displays.
Lessons, Activities, and Combat Progression · Fixes
  • Fixed blank screens after successful lessons, assistant lessons referring to slave calculations, and follow-up activities and return paths for advanced lessons.
  • Restored missing entry points in menus saved during earlier lessons and improved links to the assistant's lessons with an already hired partner.
  • Corrected companion action-point accounting in Fog Border battles, entry into some event battles, and duplicate Catfight Club win counts and participation restrictions.
  • Aligned rally entry requirements with the actual action-point cost, fixed races proceeding after entry was declined, and improved result branching for skill values outside the normal range.
  • Fixed some activities continuing to grant repeat rewards after their resources had been exhausted.
Household Management, Relationships, and Shops · Fixes
  • Fixed private rooms 2 through 4 using room 1's diet settings, along with some lesson and milk-quantity links.
  • Fixed private-room maids duplicating household duties already assigned to someone else or wasting action points.
  • Corrected dialogue references to speakers, characters being assessed, and relationship targets, and refined repeated answers and some relationship and jealousy checks.
  • Fixed missing or duplicate payments in outings and reward activities, and improved price, balance, space, and purchase-cancellation checks for groceries, furnishings, and selected procedures.
  • Aligned black-market menu requirements with actual prices and prevented character creation and payment when funds or companion space were insufficient.
Characters, Events, and Existing Progress · Fixes
  • Improved occupation modifiers, origin information, family relationships, saved backstories, and recognition of unique characters for some newly added characters.
  • Fixed rewards and purchases linking to the wrong character because of conflicting character numbers or incorrect registration data.
  • Fixed blank screens during some first meetings, progression on return visits, and the ability to purchase an already purchased character again.
  • Fixed event stages reverting and closing later choices, and progression stopping after certain equipment-wearing questions.
  • Improved startup, loading, and saved-menu refresh paths, and corrected paths that left a specific NPC scene displayed in another location.
Images, Icons, and Description Display · Fixes
  • Corrected pregnancy indicators that read another role's confirmation state, combat companions' color portraits, and Edward's sepia portrait.
  • Fixed incorrect images in daily notices, role screens, and activity buttons, corrected some face and outfit references, and improved image-path compatibility for existing saves.
  • Fixed overlapping milk prices, funds, and stock quantities, missing shop icons, medicine selection ordering, and overflowing storage lists.
  • Tidied buyer-rumor menu placement and navigation links, missing choice translations, duplicate headings, and descriptions that did not match the current state.
  • Fixed edited Meiki status immediately reverting, along with some UI borders, word spacing, and line breaks.
Small adjustments to daily life, trading, and shops
  • Tidied up gold balances on exchange and transaction screens, milk price boards, stock quantities, and potion selection.
  • Adjusted the Catfight prize to match its intended setting. Prizes have not been increased across every competition.
  • Revised buyer-rumor recommendations and return menus, guides' icons and speech, and the current contestant's displayed name.
  • Removed unnecessary information-panel headings and spacing, and improved currency notation, Korean spacing, translations, and character encoding.
  • Gave the art teacher a distinct lesson screen and icon, and tidied up equipment, storage, cheat, and character-editor displays.
In development and planned extensions
  • Agrabah special stock: small purchases of Fresh Fruit and Agrabah Wine are available at all times, with separate stored quantities and purchase tooltips. This is not a completed ingredient system that consumes these items in regular meals.
  • Further content using the hidden behavioral disposition remains an expansion area. New Dominance or Charm bonuses from cruelty or mercy are not presented as completed features in this release.
  • A full redesign of difficulty multipliers and further brothel-related plans remain for later discussion. These are separate from individual changes already applied, such as the current auction rules.
Authoring tools and distribution
  • Expanded the image checklist with MOB sets, appearance locations, and scene conditions, and improved face selection, framing, and image resizing.
  • Improved B/C image-variant condition editing and duplicate listings of backup resources. Authoring-tool improvements are not counted as additional game content.
  • Retained compatibility paths for some images referenced by older saves and organized the sources and packaging of original, personal, indie, and additional resources.
  • The game version is now 2.4.1. Acknowledgments and license notices have been updated.

New to version 2.4?

This guide covers the cumulative changes in 2.4.0 and 2.4.1 compared with 2.3. Do not overwrite the integrated release with older image packs or QSP patches. Start the game with its included EXE.
